concepts.title: Autoregressive Two-Phase Execution: Prefill vs Decode
concepts.content: LLM inference splits into parallel prefill and sequential decode. Prefill processes all prompt tokens simultaneously via dense matrix-matrix multiplications (GEMMs), saturating GPU compute cores and determining Time to First Token (TTFT). Decode generates one token per forward pass via matrix-vector multiplications (GEMVs) against the KV cache, bounding Inter-Token Latency (ITL) by HBM bandwidth.
concepts.image_prompt: Two-stage pipeline diagram showing Prompt Tokens entering a parallel Prefill GEMM block that outputs First Token and KV Cache into a sequential Decode GEMV loop emitting Output Tokens.

concepts.title: Roofline Model and Operational Intensity in LLM Serving
concepts.content: Operational intensity measures FLOPs executed per byte read from HBM. On an H100 SXM (roughly 1979 TFLOPS BF16, 3.35 TB/s HBM3), the ridge point is about 590 FLOPs/byte. Single-batch decode achieves only 1 to 2 FLOPs/byte, leaving SMs idle unless batching, speculative decoding, or quantization raises effective intensity.
concepts.image_prompt: Log-log Roofline chart plotting Operational Intensity FLOPs per Byte on horizontal axis against Throughput TFLOPS on vertical axis, marking Memory-Bound Decode on the slope and Compute-Bound Prefill on the flat roof.

concepts.title: GPU Memory Footprint Breakdown: Weights, KV Cache, Activations
concepts.content: Total VRAM equals model weights plus KV cache plus activation buffers and CUDA context overhead. A 70B model in FP16 requires 140 GB for weights alone, or 70 GB in FP8. In vLLM, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92` reserves 92% of VRAM for weights and KV blocks, leaving 8% to prevent activation OOM spikes during long prefills.
concepts.image_prompt: Stacked vertical bar diagram of GPU HBM capacity divided into Model Weights at base, Dynamic KV Cache Pool in middle, Transient Activation Workspace above, and Reserved CUDA Context at top.

concepts.title: KV Cache Mechanics and Exact Per-Token Sizing Math
concepts.content: The KV cache stores past key and value tensors across layers to avoid O(N^2) recomputation per decode step. Bytes per token equals `2 * num_layers * num_kv_heads * head_dim * dtype_bytes`. For Llama-3-70B (80 layers, 8 KV heads, 128 dim, FP16), each token consumes 327,680 bytes (320 KB), or 32 GB for 100K context.
concepts.image_prompt: Grid matrix diagram showing Layers on vertical axis and Sequence Tokens on horizontal axis, with an equation box multiplying 2, Layers, KV Heads, and Head Dim into Total KV Bytes.

concepts.title: Attention Evolution: MHA, MQA, and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
concepts.content: Multi-Head Attention (MHA) assigns each query head dedicated K and V heads, inflating KV traffic. Multi-Query Attention (MQA) shares a single KV head across all queries, hurting quality. Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) partitions queries into G groups (such as 8 KV heads for 64 query heads), cutting KV cache size and bandwidth 8x with minimal perplexity loss.
concepts.image_prompt: Three-column comparison diagram showing MHA with one-to-one Query to KV links, GQA with grouped Query heads converging on shared KV heads, and MQA with all Queries linked to one KV head.

concepts.title: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA): Low-Rank KV Compression
concepts.content: Introduced in DeepSeek-V2/V3, MLA projects keys and values into a joint low-rank latent vector `c_KV` before caching, rather than dropping KV heads. During inference, up-projection matrices are mathematically absorbed into query and output projections, and a small decoupled RoPE key vector is concatenated, shrinking KV cache footprint by over 90% versus MHA.
concepts.image_prompt: Flow diagram showing Hidden State projecting down into Compressed Latent Vector c_KV in KV Cache alongside Decoupled RoPE Key k_R, with absorbed up-projections feeding Attention Output.

concepts.title: Hybrid Linear Attention, Mamba-2 SSD, and Sliding Window KV
concepts.content: Hybrid models interleave full self-attention layers with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) or State Space Duality (Mamba-2 SSD) layers. SWA caps KV cache to a fixed local window W, while Mamba-2 maintains a constant-size recurrent state per sequence. Serving engines must manage heterogeneous memory pools combining fixed recurrent state slots and paged KV blocks.
concepts.image_prompt: Layered stack diagram alternating Fixed-Size Mamba Recurrent State blocks, Bounded Sliding Window KV blocks, and Full-Context Paged KV Attention layers along a vertical transformer pass.

concepts.title: FlashAttention-2, FlashAttention-3, and FlashAttention-4 Kernels
concepts.content: FlashAttention fuses Q*K^T, online softmax, and V multiplication inside SRAM tiles, avoiding O(N^2) HBM intermediate writes. FlashAttention-3 exploits Hopper TMA and warp-specialized ping-pong scheduling to overlap WGMMA tensor cores with softmax. FlashAttention-4 targets Blackwell SM100 large tile buffers and FP4/FP8 tensor cores; reserve extra workspace via `--mem-fraction-static 0.88`.
concepts.image_prompt: Hardware memory hierarchy diagram showing Q, K, V blocks streaming from HBM via Asynchronous TMA into On-Chip SRAM for Warp-Specialized GEMM and Online Softmax, writing final O back to HBM.

concepts.title: FlashInfer: JIT-Compiled Paged, Ragged, and Cascade Attention
concepts.content: FlashInfer is a kernel library for LLM serving supporting paged, ragged, and MLA attention across Turing through Blackwell and Rubin. It separates `plan()` (computing work distribution metadata on CPU) from `run()` (executing CUDAGraph-safe kernels) and provides Cascade Attention, which reads shared prefix KV from level-1 cache and unique suffixes from per-request pages.
concepts.image_prompt: Two-path kernel diagram showing CPU Plan Step generating Page Table Metadata into GPU Run Step, branching into Shared Prefix L1 Tile and Per-Request Suffix Paged Tiles.

concepts.title: Quantized Attention Kernels: SageAttention and FP8/FP4 Softmax
concepts.content: While weight quantization accelerates linear layers, attention remains bottlenecked by KV bandwidth at 128K+ context. SageAttention and SageAttention3 apply per-block outlier smoothing to Queries and Keys, executing Q*K^T in INT8, INT4, or microscaling FP4 and P*V in FP8. Always smooth per-channel K outliers before quantizing to prevent catastrophic attention sink collapse.
concepts.image_prompt: Pipeline diagram showing Q and K tensors passing through Outlier Smoothing and Per-Block INT4/FP4 Quantizer into Tensor Core QK GEMM, Online Softmax, and FP8 PV Accumulation.

concepts.title: PagedAttention: Virtual Memory and Block Tables for KV Cache
concepts.content: Contiguous KV pre-allocation wastes 60% to 80% of VRAM via internal and external fragmentation. PagedAttention divides the KV cache into fixed-size physical blocks (typically 16 or 32 tokens) mapped via per-sequence logical block tables. Physical blocks allocate on demand during decode and free immediately upon EOS, raising concurrent batch capacity 2x to 4x.
concepts.image_prompt: Memory mapping diagram connecting Logical Token Sequence Blocks through a Per-Request Block Table to non-contiguous Physical KV Blocks scattered across GPU HBM.

concepts.title: RadixAttention and Automatic Prefix Caching (APC)
concepts.content: Prefix caching avoids recomputing KV states for shared system prompts, RAG documents, and multi-turn chat histories. vLLM Automatic Prefix Caching hashes full KV blocks (`--enable-prefix-caching`) into an LRU hash table, whereas SGLang RadixAttention maintains a dynamic radix tree of variable-length token prefixes, splitting and evicting tree nodes via LRU reference counts.
concepts.image_prompt: Radix tree diagram with Root System Prompt node branching into Shared RAG Document node and Multi-Turn Chat branches, each pointing to retained Physical KV Cache Pages.

concepts.title: Continuous (Iteration-Level) Batching vs Static Batching
concepts.content: Static batching pads sequences to the longest request and waits for every sequence to emit EOS before starting new work, stranding GPUs on tail tokens. Continuous batching schedules at the single-iteration level: finished sequences exit the batch immediately after emitting EOS, and queued requests inject on the very next forward step.
concepts.image_prompt: Timeline grid comparing Static Batching with idle padding blocks against Iteration-Level Continuous Batching where finished sequences exit at EOS and new requests slot in immediately.

concepts.title: Chunked Prefill and Sarathi-Serve Stall-Free Scheduling
concepts.content: Long prompt prefills monopolize GPU SMs for hundreds of milliseconds, stalling concurrent decode steps and spiking Inter-Token Latency (ITL). Chunked prefill (`--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`) slices large prompts into fixed token chunks and piggybacks running decode tokens into the same mixed batch, piggybacking memory-bound decodes onto compute-dense prefill weight loads.
concepts.image_prompt: Mixed-batch token budget bar showing a Long Prompt split into three Sequential Prefill Chunks, with each chunk fused alongside Active Decode Tokens inside a single Forward Pass.

concepts.title: Zero-Overhead CPU Scheduling and vLLM V1 / SGLang Runtime
concepts.content: At sub-5ms per-token latencies, Python tokenization, block allocation, and sampler prep can exceed GPU execution time, creating GPU bubbles. Modern engines (vLLM V1 architecture and SGLang overlap scheduler) isolate the scheduler in a dedicated process and prepare metadata for step N+1 on CPU asynchronously while the GPU executes step N.
concepts.image_prompt: Dual-track timeline showing CPU Thread running Step N+1 Schedule and Metadata Prep concurrently above GPU Stream executing Step N Forward Pass with zero idle gap.

concepts.title: CUDA Graphs and torch.compile in Dynamic LLM Serving
concepts.content: Launching hundreds of small CUDA kernels per decode step incurs 3 to 10 microseconds of CPU driver overhead per kernel. Serving engines capture decode forward passes into static `CUDAGraph` objects across bucketed batch sizes (such as 1, 2, 4, 8, up to 256) and pad active batches to the nearest captured graph size.
concepts.image_prompt: Comparison diagram contrasting Uncaptured Execution with many small CPU Launch Arrows and GPU Gaps against CUDA Graph Replay launching one Combined Graph across Padded Batch Buckets.

concepts.title: Tensor Parallelism (TP): Megatron-LM Sharding and All-Reduce
concepts.content: Tensor Parallelism splits individual weight matrices across N GPUs within an NVLink domain. Attention QKV and MLP `gate_up_proj` are column-parallel, while `o_proj` and `down_proj` are row-parallel, requiring 2 `all-reduce` synchronizations per transformer layer. Avoid spanning TP across multi-node PCIe/Ethernet links where all-reduce latency bottlenecks every token.
concepts.image_prompt: Transformer layer dataflow showing Input broadcast to Column-Parallel MLP Shards across 4 GPUs, followed by Row-Parallel Shards converging into a Ring All-Reduce synchronization block.

concepts.title: Sequence Parallelism (SP) and Context Parallelism (CP / Ring Attention)
concepts.content: Sequence Parallelism splits LayerNorm and Dropout activations along the sequence dimension, replacing `all-reduce` with `reduce-scatter` and `all-gather` of equivalent volume. For 128K to 1M contexts, Context Parallelism (Ring Attention or Ulysses `all-to-all`) shards sequence tokens and KV blocks across GPUs, overlapping KV ring transfers with blockwise local attention compute.
concepts.image_prompt: Ring topology diagram of 4 GPUs holding Sequence Chunks S1 to S4, passing KV Blocks clockwise around the ring while computing local Query-Key-Value attention tiles in parallel.

concepts.title: Pipeline Parallelism (PP) and Inter-Node Micro-Batching
concepts.content: Pipeline Parallelism partitions contiguous transformer layers across nodes (`--pipeline-parallel-size`), communicating only hidden states (`batch * seq * hidden_dim`) via point-to-point `send`/`recv` over RoCE or InfiniBand. While PP tolerates slower inter-node links than TP, single-request latency suffers unless micro-batches fill the pipeline bubble across concurrent requests.
concepts.image_prompt: Four-node horizontal pipeline showing Layers 1-20 on Node 1 passing activations via Point-to-Point RDMA Send/Recv to Layers 21-40 on Node 2 across staggered Micro-Batches.

concepts.title: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Routing and Expert Parallelism (EP)
concepts.content: Sparse MoE models (such as DeepSeek-V3 671B total / 37B active) route each token to top-K routed experts plus shared experts. Expert Parallelism (`--enable-expert-parallel`) places distinct experts on different GPUs and dispatches tokens via `all-to-all` collectives, avoiding loading unused expert weights during memory-bound decode.
concepts.image_prompt: MoE layer diagram showing Token Batch entering Gating Router, fanning out via All-to-All Dispatch to specialized Expert GPUs 1 to 4, and merging via All-to-All Combine.

concepts.title: Fused MoE Kernels, Grouped GEMM, and MaskedGEMM
concepts.content: Naive MoE execution launches a separate GEMM per expert, killing GPU utilization. Fused MoE kernels permute tokens by assigned expert ID and execute a single contiguous Grouped GEMM (via CUTLASS, FlashInfer, or cuDNN Frost). During decode under Expert Parallelism, MaskedGEMM consumes fixed-shape padded buffers directly from RDMA without host synchronization.
concepts.image_prompt: Data transformation flow showing Scattered Routed Tokens sorted by a Permutation Index into Contiguous Expert Buckets, processed in one parallel Grouped GEMM kernel.

concepts.title: DeepEP and Dual-Microbatch Compute-Communication Overlap
concepts.content: In large-scale EP deployments, `all-to-all` token dispatch and combine over NVLink and RDMA can consume 40%+ of step time. DeepEP provides low-latency pure-RDMA kernels for decode and high-throughput intranode/internode forwarding for prefill, enabling dual-microbatch ping-pong overlap where microbatch A computes expert FFNs while microbatch B executes `all-to-all` network transfers.
concepts.image_prompt: Two-lane horizontal timeline showing Microbatch 0 alternating Dispatch Communication and Attention/Expert Compute in exact antiphase with Microbatch 1 to hide network latency.

concepts.title: MoE Expert Load Balancing and Dynamic Redundant Experts (EPLB)
concepts.content: Skewed production traffic routes disproportionate tokens to popular experts, turning the busiest GPU into a straggler that stalls the entire EP group. Expert Parallel Load Balancers (EPLB) track per-expert activation counters across sliding windows, periodically replicating hot experts onto spare HBM slots and updating the routing lookup table online without service interruption.
concepts.image_prompt: Cluster load diagram showing Overloaded Hot Expert on GPU 1 being replicated into a Redundant Expert Slot on GPU 3, with Router splitting traffic evenly.

concepts.title: Weight-Only Quantization: GPTQ, AWQ, and Marlin Kernels
concepts.content: In memory-bound decode, compressing weights from 16-bit to 4-bit (W4A16) cuts HBM traffic 4x while dequantizing to FP16 in registers before Tensor Core MMA. GPTQ uses Hessian second-order error compensation; AWQ scales salient weight channels based on activation magnitudes. Pair W4A16 checkpoints with Marlin kernels (`--quantization awq_marlin`) for near-roofline bandwidth.
concepts.image_prompt: Register-level pipeline showing Packed INT4 Weights and Group Scales loaded from HBM into Shared Memory, dequantized via Bitwise Lop3 in Registers, and fed with FP16 Activations into Tensor Core.

concepts.title: Weight-and-Activation Quantization: SmoothQuant and W8A8 INT8
concepts.content: Quantizing both weights and activations to 8-bit (W8A8) halves bandwidth and unlocks 2x higher INT8/FP8 Tensor Core TOPS during compute-bound prefill. Because transformer activations exhibit severe channel-wise outliers (>100x normal magnitude), SmoothQuant migrates scaling difficulty `s` from activations to weights via `Y = (X * diag(s)^-1) * (diag(s) * W)` offline.
concepts.image_prompt: Before-and-after bar chart showing spiky Activation Outliers smoothed down via Per-Channel Migration Scale factor s into Weight Matrix, feeding a unified INT8 Tensor Core GEMM.

concepts.title: FP8 Serving (E4M3/E5M2) and Block-Scaled DeepGEMM
concepts.content: Hopper and Ada GPUs natively execute FP8 E4M3 (4 exponent, 3 mantissa bits) at 2x BF16 throughput. Per-tensor static scaling degrades accuracy on outlier-heavy models; modern recipes (such as DeepSeek-V3 and DeepGEMM) quantize activations in 1x128 token tiles and weights in 128x128 blocks using fine-grained scaling factors promoted in CUDA cores between MMA steps.
concepts.image_prompt: Matrix tiling diagram showing 1x128 Activation Row Tiles multiplied against 128x128 Weight Blocks inside Tensor Core MMA, with fine-grained FP32 Scale Promotion in the epilogue.

concepts.title: Blackwell Microscaling Formats: MXFP4 and NVFP4 Serving
concepts.content: Blackwell SM100 Tensor Cores double throughput again using 4-bit floating point (E2M1). Open-standard MXFP4 shares an 8-bit power-of-two exponent (E8M0) per 32-element block, whereas NVIDIA NVFP4 uses a smaller 16-element block with FP8 E4M3 block scales plus a second-level FP32 tensor scale, preserving higher accuracy for 70B+ W4A4 inference.
concepts.image_prompt: Side-by-side bit-layout diagram comparing MXFP4 with 32 E2M1 elements sharing one E8M0 scale against NVFP4 with 16 E2M1 elements sharing an E4M3 scale and global FP32 scalar.

concepts.title: KV Cache Quantization: FP8 E4M3 and INT4 KIVI Asymmetric Scaling
concepts.content: Compressing the KV cache directly expands maximum batch size and context length. Enabling `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` in vLLM/SGLang halves KV memory with calibrated per-tensor or per-head scales. For 4-bit KV (KIVI), keys must be quantized per-channel (due to fixed channel outliers) while values are quantized per-token, keeping a short FP16 residual window.
concepts.image_prompt: Dual tensor diagram showing Key Cache quantized along Channel Columns and Value Cache quantized along Token Rows, alongside a sliding FP16 Recent Token Window.

concepts.title: Speculative Decoding: Draft-then-Verify Mechanics and Math
concepts.content: Speculative decoding runs a small draft model autoregressively for `gamma` steps, then verifies all `gamma + 1` positions in a single parallel forward pass of the target model. Rejection sampling accepts token `x` with probability `min(1, p_target(x) / p_draft(x))` and resamples from the residual distribution `(p_target - p_draft)+`, guaranteeing a mathematically lossless output distribution.
concepts.image_prompt: Loop diagram showing Draft Model proposing 4 candidate tokens sequentially, Target Model verifying all 4 in one parallel pass, Accepting 3 tokens, and Resampling token 4.

concepts.title: Tree-Based Speculative Decoding: Medusa, EAGLE-2, and EAGLE-3
concepts.content: Separate draft models suffer from vocabulary/tokenizer mismatches and high orchestration overhead. Medusa attaches multiple decoding heads to the target trunk; EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3 feed target feature states and token embeddings into a single lightweight draft transformer layer, constructing a dynamic draft token tree verified in one pass via a custom tree-attention mask.
concepts.image_prompt: Tree structure diagram showing Target Hidden State feeding an EAGLE Draft Layer that branches into a Candidate Token Tree, verified simultaneously using a 2D Tree Attention Mask.

concepts.title: Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) Native Speculative Heads
concepts.content: Instead of retrofitting external draft models post-training, architectures like DeepSeek-V3 train native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) modules directly alongside the main objective. At inference time, each lightweight MTP sequential head predicts token `t+2` conditioned on the main model's hidden representation and token `t+1`, achieving 80%+ acceptance rates with minimal extra VRAM.
concepts.image_prompt: Architecture diagram showing Main Transformer Trunk emitting Token t+1 and passing Hidden State h_t into a chained MTP Head that predicts Speculative Token t+2 for verification.

concepts.title: Speculative Decoding Roofline Cliff and Dynamic Batch Cutoff
concepts.content: Speculative decoding converts idle memory-bound decode capacity into parallel verification compute. However, verification multiplies per-request FLOPs by `gamma + 1`. Above batch sizes of 32 to 64, target verification pushes the GPU into the compute-bound regime where extra draft tokens increase latency; configure `--speculative-disable-by-batch-size 32` to bypass speculation under heavy load.
concepts.image_prompt: Line chart plotting Speedup Factor against Concurrent Batch Size, showing 2.5x speedup at Batch 1 dropping across a Roofline Cliff below 1.0x past Batch 32 Cutoff.

concepts.title: Prefill-Decode (PD) Disaggregation Architecture
concepts.content: Collocating compute-heavy prefill and bandwidth-bound decode on the same GPUs causes prefill spikes to violate decode ITL SLOs, while forcing uniform TP/EP sizing. PD disaggregation (DistServe, Splitwise, llm-d) splits serving into dedicated Prefill Pods (optimized for TTFT at high compute utilization) and Decode Pods (optimized for large batches and low ITL).
concepts.image_prompt: Cluster architecture diagram showing Request Router sending Prompts to a Compute-Optimized Prefill GPU Pool, transferring KV Cache over RDMA to a Bandwidth-Optimized Decode GPU Pool streaming tokens.

concepts.title: KV Cache Handoff Fabrics: NIXL, GPUDirect RDMA, and UCCL
concepts.content: PD disaggregation requires transferring multi-megabyte KV caches from prefill to decode nodes in single-digit milliseconds. NVIDIA NIXL (`NixlConnector`) abstracts point-to-point zero-copy transfers over GPUDirect RDMA (InfiniBand or RoCEv2) and NVLink, using pull-based one-sided RDMA READs so decode workers fetch paged KV blocks without interrupting prefill GPU kernels.
concepts.image_prompt: Network dataflow diagram showing Decode GPU issuing a One-Sided RDMA Read via NIXL Connector across an InfiniBand/RoCE Switch directly into Prefill GPU HBM Page Blocks.

concepts.title: KV-Centric Distributed Caching: Mooncake Store and LMCache
concepts.content: When GPU HBM fills up on multi-turn agentic or long-context RAG workloads, recomputing evicted KV prefixes wastes prefill FLOPs. LMCache and Mooncake Store aggregate underutilized CPU DRAM, local NVMe SSDs, and remote RDMA memory into a cluster-wide content-addressed L2/L3 KV pool, matching prefix hashes globally across all vLLM/SGLang replicas.
concepts.image_prompt: Three-tier storage hierarchy showing GPU HBM L1 Paged Cache connected via PCIe/RDMA to Node DRAM L2 Pool and Distributed NVMe/Mooncake Store L3 Cluster Pool.

concepts.title: Constrained and Structured Decoding: XGrammar and Outlines
concepts.content: Enforcing JSON schemas or context-free grammars during generation requires masking invalid vocabulary logits before sampling. Naive regex evaluation per token on CPU stalls the GPU. XGrammar and Outlines compile schemas into pushdown automata or FSMs, precomputing vocabulary bitmasks for deterministic state transitions and overlapping context-dependent mask generation on CPU with GPU decode.
concepts.image_prompt: State machine diagram showing JSON Schema compiled into a Pushdown Automaton, emitting a Vocabulary Bitmask Tensor that zeroes invalid logits before the GPU Softmax Sampler.

concepts.title: Multi-LoRA Serving at Scale: Punica and S-LoRA Unified Paging
concepts.content: Serving hundreds of fine-tuned LoRA adapters from one base model avoids duplicating base weights in VRAM. Punica and S-LoRA store dynamic rank matrices (`A` and `B`) alongside KV blocks in a unified paged memory pool, computing `W*x` in a shared batched GEMM and adding heterogeneous adapter residuals via custom Segmented Gather-Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SGMV/BGMV) kernels.
concepts.image_prompt: Parallel compute diagram showing Input Batch passing through Shared Base Weight GEMM on left and Unified Paged LoRA Adapter Pool via BGMV Kernel on right, summed at output.

concepts.title: Test-Time Compute Scaling and Reasoning Model Serving
concepts.content: Reasoning models (such as DeepSeek-R1 and o3-class architectures) generate thousands of internal chain-of-thought tokens per request or sample N parallel trajectories for Best-of-N verification. This shifts workloads from prefill-heavy to extreme decode-heavy regimes, requiring prefix tree sharing (RadixAttention) so parallel reasoning branches share the prompt KV cache with zero duplication.
concepts.image_prompt: Branching trajectory diagram showing a Single Shared Prompt KV Prefix fanning out into 8 Parallel Reasoning Chain-of-Thought Branches evaluated by a Verifier Scoring Block.

concepts.title: Agentic Trajectory Serving and Storage Bandwidth Bottlenecks
concepts.content: Autonomous coding and computer-use agents run 20 to 100+ turn loops where each turn appends tool outputs to a growing 64K+ token history. Because tool execution pauses last seconds to minutes, GPU KV blocks get evicted; systems like DualPath and Mooncake pin session KV states in host DRAM/NVMe and prefetch them asynchronously when tool calls return.
concepts.image_prompt: Cyclic loop diagram showing LLM Decode emitting a Tool Call, offloading Session KV to Host DRAM during External Tool Execution, and prefetching KV back before the next Turn.

concepts.title: Multimodal Vision-Language Serving: Encoder-Prefill-Decode (EPD)
concepts.content: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) run a ViT vision encoder on image/video patches before projecting visual tokens into the LLM prefill. Because ViT compute is dense and image tokens are reusable across turns, EPD disaggregation isolates ViT encoding onto dedicated Encoder pods and caches projected image embeddings in a cross-node store (`vLLM-Omni` / Mooncake).
concepts.image_prompt: Three-stage disaggregated pipeline showing Image Patches entering Vision Encoder Pool, writing Visual Embeddings to Shared Cache, followed by LLM Prefill Pool and LLM Decode Pool.

concepts.title: Core LLM Serving SLOs: TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and Goodput
concepts.content: Average throughput hides tail latency violations. Production SLOs track Time to First Token (TTFT, bounded by queueing + prefill), Time Per Output Token (TPOT, average decode pace), and P99 Inter-Token Latency (ITL, spotting chunked-prefill stalls). Goodput measures completed requests per second that strictly satisfy both `P95 TTFT < X` and `P99 ITL < Y` simultaneously.
concepts.image_prompt: Request timeline gauge showing Request Arrival to First Token labeled TTFT, gaps between subsequent tokens labeled ITL, and a Goodput Filter rejecting traces that breach P99 thresholds.

concepts.title: KV-Cache-Aware Routing and Load Balancing: llm-d and AIBrix
concepts.content: Round-robin or least-connections load balancers destroy prefix cache hit rates by scattering multi-turn sessions across stateless replicas. KV-aware routers (such as llm-d, Dynamo Router, and vLLM Production Stack) maintain a global prefix-hash directory or consistent hash ring balanced against real-time GPU KV block utilization (`vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc`) to maximize locality without overloading hot pods.
concepts.image_prompt: Smart router diagram inspecting Incoming Prompt Prefix Hash and querying Replica KV Cache Hit Ratio and Queue Depth before routing to Worker 2 with Cached Prefix.

concepts.title: Autoscaling LLM Fleets on Kubernetes: KEDA and Cold-Start Mitigation
concepts.content: CPU and memory metrics never trigger on LLM saturation because prefill/decode pre-allocates 90%+ VRAM at startup. Configure KEDA ScaledObjects on Prometheus metrics `vllm:num_requests_waiting` and `vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc`. To cut 100GB+ checkpoint cold starts from minutes to seconds, stream safetensors directly from local NVMe or RDMA tensor caches via `runai-model-streamer`.
concepts.image_prompt: Control loop diagram showing vLLM exporting Waiting Queue and KV Usage metrics to Prometheus, triggering KEDA HPA to launch a New GPU Pod loading weights via Fast Tensor Streamer.

concepts.title: GPU Hardware Observability, Xid Errors, and Silent Data Corruption
concepts.content: Monitor GPU fleet health via `dcgm-exporter` scraping `DCGM_FI_DEV_SM_CLOCK`, `DCGM_FI_DEV_MEM_COPY_utilization`, and `DCGM_FI_DEV_NVLINK_CRC_FLIT_ERROR_COUNT`. Alert immediately on `DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS` (such as Xid 79 fallen off bus, Xid 48/63 double-bit ECC, or Xid 140 unrecovered NVLink error) via Kubernetes Node Problem Detector to cordon degraded nodes before silent corruption ruins generations.
concepts.image_prompt: Observability dashboard diagram connecting GPU NVLink and HBM ECC Counters through DCGM Exporter to Prometheus Alertmanager, triggering Node Cordon on Xid 79 or 63 faults.

concepts.title: Production Engine Selection: vLLM vs SGLang vs TensorRT-LLM
concepts.content: In 2026, all three engines share PagedAttention, continuous batching, and FP8/FP4 support. Choose vLLM for broad model coverage (200+ architectures) and multi-vendor hardware (NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, TPU); choose SGLang for shared-prefix agentic/RAG trees (RadixAttention) and native DeepSeek MoE/PD disaggregation; choose TensorRT-LLM for maximum single-model NVFP4 throughput on Blackwell rack-scale deployments.
concepts.image_prompt: Decision matrix comparing Plain Labeled Boxes for vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM across axes of Hardware Breadth, Shared-Prefix Agentic Reuse, and Peak Blackwell NVFP4 Performance.
